questions.question: A neonate is being examined after delivery. The delivery was complicated by shoulder dystocia which led to the injury of the upper trunk of the brachial plexus. Which of the following deformities is least likely to be seen in this neonate?

options.text: Abduction and medial rotation at shoulder joint
Sensory loss along the outer aspect of the arm

suspectLines.text: Upper trunk injury causes Erb or Erb-Duchenne palsy. It produces adduction and medial rotation at the shoulder, not abduction. The usual mechanism is excessive separation of head and neck, including birth injury, damaging C5-C6. Affected nerves include suprascapular, axillary, musculocutaneous, and radial nerves. The classic waiter's-tip posture includes arm adducted and medially rotated, elbow extended, forearm pronated, and sensory loss along the outer aspect of the arm.

questions.question: A 40-year-old man has a C6, C7 nerve root injury due to disc herniation. Sensations of which part of the upper limb will be lost?

suspectLines.text: With C6 and C7 root injury, sensation over the thumb and index finger is lost. The palmar pad of the thumb is supplied by C6 and the pad of the index finger by C7.

questions.question: You are testing the deep tendon reflexes in a patient with Guillain-Barre syndrome. Which spinal segment is tested predominantly by a tap on the triceps tendon?

suspectLines.text: Tapping the triceps tendon posterior to the elbow predominantly tests C7. Tapping the biceps tendon in the cubital fossa predominantly tests C6.

questions.explanation: Tapping the triceps tendon posterior to the elbow predominantly tests C7. Tapping the biceps tendon in the cubital fossa predominantly tests C6.
